title: Patient Payment Plans Credit Schedule: Grace, Delinquency, Cure and Default Thresholds
content:
This credit schedule fixes, for each tier of the Patient Payment Plans, the grace allowed on an installment, the counts of missed installments that make a plan delinquent or default it, the cure window, and the lead times of the related notices.

| Tier | Grace days after a due date | Missed installments that make the plan delinquent | Missed installments (counted since the plan was last current) that default the plan | Cure window (calendar days after the plan becomes delinquent) | Notice of a miss sent within (calendar days) | Default warning sent before the cure window ends (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3-Month Interest-Free Plan | 10 | 1 | 2 | 30 | 3 | 10 |
| 6-Month Interest-Free Plan | 10 | 1 | 2 | 30 | 3 | 10 |
| 12-Month Interest-Free Plan | 10 | 1 | 2 | 30 | 3 | 10 |
| 18-Month Extended Plan | 10 | 1 | 3 | 30 | 3 | 10 |
| 24-Month Extended Plan | 10 | 1 | 3 | 30 | 3 | 10 |
| Financial Hardship Plan | 15 | 1 | 3 | 45 | 3 | 10 |

**Definitions carried by the schedule.**

- *Grace days* are calendar days after an installment's due date before it counts as missed.
- *Cure window* is the number of calendar days after the plan becomes delinquent within which paying every missed installment returns it to active.
- The count that defaults a plan is the number of missed installments counted since the plan last was current.

**Comparisons within the schedule.**

- A single missed installment makes a plan delinquent on every tier.
- The three Interest-Free tiers default at 2 missed installments; the 18-Month Extended Plan, the 24-Month Extended Plan and the Financial Hardship Plan default at 3.
- The Financial Hardship Plan allows 15 grace days and a 45-day cure window; every other tier allows 10 grace days and a 30-day cure window.
